findings.issue: Sense-changing mistranslation: こらしめてやる means 'I'll punish him / teach him a lesson' (こらしめる = chastise, discipline). Nothing in the Japanese means 'shoot'. The pt ('Vou dar uma lição nele!') and lit fields are correct; en contradicts them.
findings.current: I'm gonna shoot him.
findings.suggested: I'll teach him a lesson!
findings.fix: I'll teach him a lesson!
notes: Tatoeba does link 'I'm gonna shoot him' (loose Tanaka pair; orig. 'shoot him down'=chastise per Tatoeba comment). こらしめる=punish, never shoot; en contradicts pt/lit/expl/tokens.
Tatoeba does link this EN (loose Tanaka pair, flagged in Tatoeba comments), but こらしめてやる means 'punish/teach a lesson' — no 'shoot'. EN contradicts pt/lit/expl/token glosses; fix is correct.

findings.issue: Wrong reading of 何: standalone sentence-final 何 in だから何？ is read なに (なん only before だ/で/と/の or counters, e.g. 何だ). Standard reading is だからなに.
findings.current: だからなん?
findings.suggested: だからなに?
findings.fix: だからなに?
notes: Tatoeba's own transcription is だから[何|なに]？. Bare sentence-final 何 reads なに; なん only before だ/で/と/の or counters. Suggested kana keeps the batch's ASCII '?' convention.
Standalone sentence-final 何 is なに; なん only before だ/で/と/の or counters (per JA-teaching refs, kanjifumi.jp). だから何？＝だからなに. なん is a genuine reading error, not a style choice.

findings.issue: Token reading for 何 is なん, but with no following copula/counter (だから何？) the reading is なに.
findings.current: なん
findings.suggested: なに
findings.fix: なに
notes: Same misreading at token level: tokens[2] (何) must be なに in bare final position with no copula/counter following.
Same rule at token level: nothing follows 何 in だから何？, so tokens[2].r must be なに. Record's own expl groups 何 with 誰/どこ as the interrogative なに.

findings.issue: Same wrong reading propagated to romaji: should reflect だからなに (dakara nani), not なん.
findings.current: dakaranan?
findings.suggested: dakaranani?
findings.fix: dakaranani?
notes: Propagation of the same misreading; 'dakaranani?' matches the batch romaji style (lowercase, no spaces).
Propagation of the same reading error; 'dakaranani?' matches the corpus space-less romaji convention (cf. korashimeteyaru., donokuraiitano?).

findings.issue: Inaccurate literal mirror: uses 'you' while en/pt/lit_pt target 'him'; 'go and' implies a motion verb absent from the JP (やる = do-to-someone, not go); 'a good talking-to' (verbal scolding) undertranslates こらしめる (punish).
findings.current: I'll go and give you a good talking-to.
findings.suggested: I'll punish (him) / teach (him) a lesson [〜てやる: determined].
findings.fix: I'll punish (him) / teach (him) a lesson.
notes: Field is contractually literal but is a free rendering: 'you' clashes with him/nele in en/pt/lit_pt; 'go and' maps to nothing in JP; 'talking-to' undertranslates こらしめる (token gloss: punish).
'go and' fabricates a motion verb absent from てやる; 'you' contradicts the record-wide 'him'; 'a good talking-to' (verbal only) undersells こらしめる. Bracket style of fix matches batch (tatoeba-4772).

findings.issue: The parenthetical '(ir e)' suggests the JP contains a motion verb ('go and'); やる in 〜てやる means 'fazer (a alguém)', not 'ir'. Misleads about the literal structure.
findings.current: Vou (ir e) puni-lo / dar-lhe um corretivo.
findings.suggested: Vou puni-lo / dar-lhe um corretivo.
findings.fix: Vou puni-lo / dar-lhe um corretivo.
notes: '(ir e)' asserts a motion verb the JP lacks; auxiliary やる in てやる = 'fazer (a alguém)', not 'ir'. It mirrors lit_en's bogus 'go and'; dropping it is correct.
'(ir e)' claims an implied motion verb the JP lacks — やる in てやる is do-to-someone, never 'ir'. Parentheses convention marks genuinely implied elements; must be fixed together with lit_en.

findings.issue: '(it)' implies an inanimate subject, but いた is the animate verb いる ('you/he stayed'); the item's own expl and en ('How long did you stay?') confirm an animate subject. lit_pt has no such '(it)'.
findings.current: How long (a time) was (it)?
findings.suggested: How long (a time) were (you) (there)?
findings.fix: How long (a time) were (you) (there)?
notes: いた is animate いる ('you stayed', per item's en and expl); '(it)' implies an inanimate copular reading (〜だった) and contradicts the animacy point taught. Suggested fix fits the paren convention.
いた is animate いる (record's own expl: 'para seres animados'; en: 'did you stay'). '(it)' misidentifies the elided subject and undermines the very animacy point the item teaches; lit_pt avoids it.

findings.issue: The verb of いびきをかく is misidentified as 書く ('to write'). The idiom uses かく = 掻く (normally written in kana), not 書く. This teaches a false verb/kanji identity to learners.
findings.current: We take the verb 書く/かく (here かく in the sense of 'to snore', いびきをかく = 'to snore')
findings.suggested: We take the verb かく (掻く, usually written in kana — not 書く 'to write'; いびきをかく = 'to snore')
findings.fix: We take the verb かく (掻く, usually written in kana — not 書く 'to write'; いびきをかく = 'to snore')
notes: いびきをかく is かく=掻く (kana-preferred, as in 汗をかく/あぐらをかく), not 書く 'write'. Explanation asserts a false verb/kanji identity; suggested fix is correct.
いびきをかく uses 掻く (kana-preferred) per Daijisen/JMdict; 書く means 'to write'. False verb identity taught to learners; suggested fix is accurate.

findings.issue: Same false fact as expl_en: the verb of いびきをかく is identified as 書く ('escrever'); it is actually かく = 掻く (normalmente em kana), unrelated to 書く.
findings.current: Tomamos o verbo 書く/かく (aqui かく no sentido de 'roncar', いびきをかく = 'roncar')
findings.suggested: Tomamos o verbo かく (掻く, normalmente em kana — não 書く 'escrever'; いびきをかく = 'roncar')
findings.fix: Tomamos o verbo かく (掻く, normalmente em kana — não 書く 'escrever'; いびきをかく = 'roncar')
notes: Same hard factual error on the pt side ('escrever'); must be fixed in lockstep with expl_en.
Same false fact in pt-BR explanation: the verb is かく=掻く, not 書く 'escrever'. Fix mirrors the expl_en correction.

findings.issue: 質問がある is existential ('a silly question exists'), but the literal renders it as a copula ('That's a silly question'), misrepresenting the structure the literal field must mirror. lit_pt correctly uses 'existe'.
findings.current: That's a silly (adjectival) question, it's just that.
findings.suggested: A silly (adjectival) question exists, it's just that.
findings.fix: A silly (adjectival) question exists, it's just that.
notes: がある is existential; lit_en's 'That's a silly question' renders バカな質問だ instead, contradicting the sentence's own expl_en ('there is a question') and lit_pt ('existe-é-que').
質問がある is existential; lit_en's copular 'That's a silly question' contradicts lit_pt ('existe') and the expl fields. Literal field must mirror structure.

findings.issue: 'Já não gosto' is European-Portuguese-leaning phrasing; natural Brazilian Portuguese for もう〜ない in this casual register is 'não... mais'.
findings.current: Já não gosto (de você).
findings.suggested: Não gosto mais (de você).
findings.fix: Não gosto mais (de você).
notes: Style contract: natural pt-BR, never pt-PT, casual register. Bare 'já não gosto' reads Lusitanian/literary; corpus siblings use 'não ... mais' (e.g. tatoeba-4860). 'Não gosto mais (de você)' is right.
'Já não' is EP-leaning/literary; project contract requires natural casual pt-BR, and sibling tatoeba-4816 in this batch already uses 'não ... mais'. 4852 is the outlier.

findings.issue: Gloss 'isn't it, no' fits the tag-question/standalone use of ない, not this sentence, where ない is plain negation in 好きじゃない. Elsewhere in the corpus this token is glossed 'not (negation)'.
findings.current: isn't it, no
findings.suggested: not (negation)
findings.fix: not (negation)
notes: 'isn't it, no' is the tag-question sense of じゃない?; here ない is declarative negation. Corpus convention is 'not (negation)' (335 occurrences vs 2 of this gloss).
ない here is plain negation completing じゃない; 'isn't it, no' is the tag-question sense and misleads. Batch convention glosses this token 'not (negation)' (4 other sentences).

findings.issue: Gloss 'não é, não' attributes the copular sense to ない alone; in 好きじゃない this token is the plain negation, glossed elsewhere as 'não (negação)'.
findings.current: não é, não
findings.suggested: não (negação)
findings.fix: não (negação)
notes: pt mirror of the same wrong sense; 'não (negação)' matches the corpus-wide convention and the en fix.
Same defect in pt gloss: 'não é, não' implies tag use; corpus convention is 'não (negação)'.

findings.issue: Particle を left as を instead of the corpus phonetic convention お (romaji already has 'ibikio...'); inconsistent with the は→わ / へ→え handling applied elsewhere in the corpus.
findings.current: いびきをかいたことがある?
findings.suggested: いびきおかいたことがある?
findings.fix: kana: いびきおかいたことがある? AND tokens[1].r: を → お (both must match the phonetic convention, as done for は→わ and へ→え elsewhere in the batch)
notes: Convention を→お is intentional and applied to は/へ in this same batch (both kana and token r); romaji already has 'ibikio'. Fix must include the token reading too.
Corpus kana keeps を everywhere (1447 kana fields, e.g. ははわ…ふくをきている); を→お applies to romaji only. Current kana matches convention — the fix would create the outlier.

findings.issue: 日本 transcribed にっぽん; in this plain conversational wish sentence the standard reading is にほん (にっぽん is formal/emphatic contexts). tokens[0].r and romaji ('nippon' → 'nihon') need the matching fix.
findings.current: にっぽんえいけたらいいのに。
findings.suggested: にほんえいけたらいいのに。
findings.fix: にほんえいけたらいいのに。
notes: Corpus vocab registry itself lemmatizes 日本 as にほん (にっぽん only alt form), so にっぽん breaks graph consistency; にほん is the standard reading in this plain conversational sentence. Fix kana + tokens[0].r + romaji.
Corpus reads bare 日本 as にほん everywhere except 3 MeCab-artifact sentences; casual 〜たらいいのに wish takes standard にほん. Cascade to tokens[0].r and romaji as the finding states.

findings.issue: Wrong reading: 何 before を is read なに, never なん (なん appears only before だ/で/と/counters). The kana teaches なんを for 何をしたら.
findings.current: もうなんをしたらいいかわからない。
findings.suggested: もうなにをしたらいいかわからない。
findings.fix: もうなにをしたらいいかわからない。
notes: 何 before を is なに in standard Japanese; なんを is not a valid reading here. Kana field teaches a wrong reading.
何を is always なにを; なん occurs only before d/t/n sounds and counters. Kana teaches a nonexistent reading なんを.

findings.issue: Token reading for 何 is なん, but before を it must be なに in this sentence.

Same defect at token level: tokens[1] (何) r must be なに before を.

findings.issue: Wrong reading: 何をしてた is read なにをしてた; なんを is not a valid reading of 何を.

findings.suggested: なにをしてたとおもう?
findings.fix: なにをしてたとおもう?
notes: 何をしてた reads なにをしてた; kana なんを is wrong. Suggested fix correctly keeps the existing ASCII '?'.
なにをしてた is the only valid reading; なんを is not real Japanese.

findings.issue: Token reading for 何 is なん, but before を it must be なに.

Token r なん wrong before を; must be なに.

findings.issue: 外国人 means 'foreigners' (people), not 'foreign countries' (that would be 外国); sense-changing lexical error in the literal gloss. lit_pt and tokens are correct.

findings.fix: As for foreigners, they're interesting, huh.

外国人 = people, not countries; lit_en contradicts en, lit_pt, and the token gloss 'foreigner(s)'. Sense-changing.

findings.issue: 持ってる is possession ('still have/hold it'), not existence/remainder: 'Is there still some left' misrepresents the structure the literal field must mirror. lit_pt ('Ainda tendo') is correct.
findings.current: Is there still some left (could there be?) (I don't know, hmm.)
findings.suggested: Whether (I) still have (it) — (I) don't know, hmm.
findings.fix: Whether (I) still have (it) — (I) don't know, hmm.
notes: 持ってる is possession, not existence/remainder; lit_en breaks the literal-mirror contract and contradicts the token gloss. lit_pt is fine.
持ってる is possession; existential 'Is there still some left' rewrites verb and argument structure in a deliberately-literal field. lit_pt 'Ainda tendo' shows the intended mirror.

findings.issue: また ('again') is dropped: the JP says the speaker will once more run like the wind. pt keeps it ('de novo'), lit_en keeps it ('again'), and the また token is glossed 'again', so en is inconsistent and loses the resumptive sense.
findings.current: Someday I'll run like the wind.
findings.suggested: Someday I'll run like the wind again.
findings.fix: Someday I'll run like the wind again.
notes: また is semantically load-bearing and kept by pt, lit_en, and the token gloss; en dropping 'again' loses the resumptive sense and is internally inconsistent.
また is a content word kept by pt ('de novo'), lit_en ('again'), and the token gloss; en alone drops the resumptive sense — real omission, not translation license.

findings.issue: Etymology stated backwards: おめでとう derives FROM めでたい (お+めでたく with u-onbin), it is not the 'origin of' めでたい. expl_pt mirrors the same reversed wording ('origem do adjetivo めでたい') and needs the same fix ('derivada do adjetivo').
findings.current: おめでとう is an interjection (origin of the adjective めでたい, 'auspicious')
findings.suggested: おめでとう is an interjection (derived from the adjective めでたい, 'auspicious')
findings.fix: おめでとう is an interjection (derived from the adjective めでたい, 'auspicious')
notes: Derivation is おめでとう ← めでたい (お+めでたく, u-onbin); 'origin of the adjective めでたい' states it backwards. expl_pt 'origem do adjetivo' needs the mirrored fix.
おめでとう < お+めでたく with u-onbin (cf. ありがとう < ありがたく); 'origin of めでたい' inverts the derivation. expl_pt needs the same fix.

findings.issue: Self-contradictory: ございます already contains ます, so ます cannot 'attach to ございます'; it attaches to the stem ござい (of ござる), as the token note correctly states. expl_pt has the same wording ('se anexa ao auxiliar ございます') and needs the same fix.
findings.current: ます (the polite verb ending) attaches to the auxiliary ございます
findings.suggested: ます (the polite verb ending) attaches to ござい, the stem of ござる
findings.fix: ます (the polite verb ending) attaches to ござい, the stem of ござる
notes: ございます already contains ます, so 'ます attaches to ございます' is self-contradictory; the token note correctly attaches ます to ござい (連用形 of ござる).
ございます = ござい+ます, so 'ます attaches to ございます' is circular; the ござい token note states the correct attachment. expl_pt needs the same fix.

findings.issue: と here is the quotative particle, not a 'partícula final' (sentence-final particle class like よ/ね); the label teaches a wrong particle category. expl_en correctly says just 'The particle と'.
findings.current: A partícula final と liga essa oração ao verbo 思う ('achar').
findings.suggested: A partícula と liga essa oração ao verbo 思う ('achar').
findings.fix: A partícula と liga essa oração ao verbo 思う ('achar').
notes: と before 思う is quotative, not 終助詞; 'partícula final' is the fixed pt-BR term for sentence-final particles and mislabels the category. expl_en has no 'final'.
'Partícula final' = 終助詞 class term (used for よ elsewhere in this batch); quotative と mislabeled. Dropping 'final' matches expl_en.

findings.issue: JP is a wh-question (どれくらい = 'how much/how long', and どれ is the stated grammar target), but pt renders it as a yes/no question ('vai demorar muito?'), changing the question type and hiding the interrogative being taught. expl_pt itself glosses it as 'quanto tempo'.
findings.current: Será que vai demorar muito?
findings.suggested: Quanto tempo será que vai levar?
findings.fix: Quanto tempo será que vai levar?
notes: どれくらい asks quantity; 'vai demorar muito?' is a yes/no question, hiding the taught wh-word どれ and contradicting en and expl_pt ('quanto tempo'). Suggested fix is natural pt-BR.
JP asks 'how much/long' (wh); pt asks yes/no 'demorar muito?'. Contradicts expl_pt's own 'quanto tempo' gloss and hides target どれ. Suggested pt is natural.

findings.issue: Wrong reason for the missing copula: だ is absent because plain だ is regularly dropped before か/かい after any noun/na-adjective, not because 同じ 'functions as the predicate' (as a plain statement it would be 同じだ).
findings.current: Note that there is no だ before かい because 同じ functions as the predicate.
findings.suggested: Note that there is no だ before かい: the plain copula だ is normally dropped before か/かい.
findings.fix: Note that there is no だ before かい: the plain copula だ is normally dropped before か/かい.
notes: Causal claim is false: as a statement the predicate takes だ (同じだ). Absence is the regular だ-drop before か/かい after nouns/na-adjectives, as the fix states.
expl_en: reason is wrong — 同じ is the predicate in 同じだ too, with だ. だ drops before か/かい after any nominal predicate (学生かい, 元気かい); nothing specific to 同じ.

findings.issue: Same wrong grammar reason as expl_en: the absence of だ is due to the general rule that だ is omitted before か/かい, not to 同じ 'funcionar como predicado' (a afirmação simples seria 同じだ).
findings.current: Repare que não há だ antes de かい porque 同じ funciona como o predicado.
findings.suggested: Repare que não há だ antes de かい: a cópula だ normalmente é omitida antes de か/かい.
findings.fix: Repare que não há だ antes de かい: a cópula だ normalmente é omitida antes de か/かい.
notes: Same wrong causal claim as expl_en; the general だ-drop rule before か/かい is the real reason.
expl_pt: same wrong causal rule as expl_en; the plain statement would be 同じだ. Correct rule is だ-omission before か/かい.

findings.suggested: なかっ- (past stem of ない) + たら = なかったら ("if there isn't / without")
findings.fix: なかっ- (past stem of ない) + たら = なかったら ("if there isn't / without")
notes: 'なかった + たら' concatenates to *なかったたら and contradicts the record's own なかっ|たら token split; formula is the lesson's core morphology, must be exact.
expl_en: 'なかった+たら' concatenates to *なかったたら and contradicts the record's own token split なかっ|たら. Fix aligns with tokens; なかった+ら also valid.

findings.issue: Same formula error as expl_en: 'なかった + たら' duplica o た e produziria *なかったたら; a segmentação correta é なかっ + たら (como nos tokens) ou なかった + ら.
findings.current: なかった (passado de ない, "não existir") + たら = なかったら
findings.suggested: なかっ- (radical do passado de ない) + たら = なかったら ("se não houver / sem")
findings.fix: なかっ- (radical do passado de ない) + たら = なかったら ("se não houver / sem")
notes: Same double-counted た as expl_en; fix matches the token notes' なかっ- segmentation.

findings.issue: 'aquilo/aqueles (coisas distantes do falante)' maps それ onto あれ; pt-BR mirrors the JP three-way system (これ=isto/este, それ=isso/esse, あれ=aquilo/aquele), and here それら is anaphoric.

findings.issue: Stray opening parenthesis before 'is judged' (with a matching stray ')' at the very end of the field) breaks the sentence; the main clause is wrongly swallowed into a parenthetical.

Real defect, but the proposed fix leaves the trailing ')' orphaned; the '(' belongs before 'The verb'.

findings.issue: Direction ambiguous: リンクフリー means others may freely link TO this page; 'livre para colocar links' reads as placing links on the page.

findings.issue: Bracketed implied referent is wrong: lit_en says '[to him]' while en/pt both (correctly, per the default reading) render the implied object as 'me' ('Don't talk to me' / 'Não fale comigo'). The literal field contradicts the sentence's own translations.

findings.issue: Unfaithful translation: 話があるんだけど says 'there's something (I want to talk about)...'; 'in private' is nowhere in the Japanese, and the statement is turned into an explicit request. pt and lit_en are faithful; en is the outlier.

en is Layer-A Tatoeba source English, not AI output (see research/derived/tr/full/batch_0001.json: jp+en given, only nat/lit generated; pt_validated_against='en'). Not ours to rewrite.

findings.issue: Editing artifact: duplicated word in the parenthetical '(o alvo alvo)'; should be '(o alvo)'. expl_en has no such parenthetical.

'(o alvo alvo)' is a clear duplicated-word editing artifact; expl_en has no counterpart. '(alvo)' is the convention used elsewhere (cf. 77564 expl_pt).

findings.issue: Literal mirror misrepresents the particle: 練習が is a が-marked subject, but 'As for practice' is this corpus's topic-は device (cf. sent:tatoeba-77200 lit_en 'The conversation (subject) strayed' for the same particle). The expl itself correctly says が marks the subject.
findings.current: As for practice, it produces completion/perfection.
findings.suggested: Practice (subject) produces completion/perfection.
findings.fix: Practice (subject) produces completion/perfection.
notes: 'As for' is this corpus's は device; 練習 is が-marked and 77200 in the same batch mirrors が as '(subject)'. Contradicts its own expl.
'As for' is this corpus's は device (used only for は across the tr batches); 練習が is が-marked. Misrepresents は/が, the course's core contrast, and contradicts its own expl.

findings.issue: Same defect in Portuguese: 'Quanto à prática' applies the topic-は teaching device to a が-marked subject, contradicting the expl (which correctly calls 練習が sujeito) and the corpus convention of marking が as '(sujeito)'.
findings.current: Quanto à prática, (ela) gera a conclusão/perfeição.
findings.suggested: A prática (sujeito) gera a conclusão/perfeição.
findings.fix: A prática (sujeito) gera a conclusão/perfeição.
notes: Same defect in pt: 'Quanto à' is the は device (cf. 77309/77447/774692), while 77200 mirrors が as '(sujeito)'. expl_pt itself calls 練習が sujeito.
Same defect: 'Quanto à' is reserved for は throughout the corpus; が sentences render as '(sujeito)' (cf. 77200 'Conversa (sujeito) desviou'). 77424 is the outlier.

findings.issue: POS mismatch in gloss: 愚か is a na-adjective (the token note says so), but 'fool' is a noun; the adjectival gloss is 'foolish'. The pt gloss 'tolo / bobo' works as adjective and is fine.

愚か is a na-adjective (the token's own note says 形状詞); 'fool' is a noun (that would be 愚か者). JMdict glosses it foolish/stupid/silly. Wrong-POS gloss.

findings.issue: 〜と思います states an opinion ('I think/believe'); 'I insist' overstates the illocutionary force (would be 主張します) and contradicts expl_en/expl_pt, which gloss 思います as 'I think / I believe that'.

findings.suggested: I think exceptions shouldn't be made.

en is the authoritative Tatoeba English pair; batch-wide house style keeps loose idiomatic en ('I feel lethargic', 'I'm glad to hear that'). lit_en/expl/pt all carry the accurate 思います force.

findings.issue: Subject rendered as first person ('I'm doing well') while en/pt and the record's adopted reading are second person ('You are doing very well'); lit_pt correctly leaves the subject omitted. Internal person contradiction confuses learners.

findings.suggested: (You) are doing well, you know.
findings.fix: (You) are doing well, you know.

Real internal contradiction: lit_en says 'I' while en/pt and lit_pt take the omitted subject as second person; よ also points at the listener.

findings.issue: Corpus phonetic convention writes the object particle を as お; here を is retained (かれを), inconsistent with the convention (cf. は→わ applied in 77679) and with this item's own romaji 'kareo'.

findings.fix: ちからいっぱいかれおたたいた。
notes: Corpus convention keeps を in kana: 1447/1447 sentences across all 371 batches retain it, 0 replaced. Romaji 'o' is just standard Hepburn, not evidence of a kana rule.
Corpus-wide convention: kana keeps を (1447/1447 occurrences across 371 batches, zero converted). Only romaji renders it 'o'. Current kana is correct.

findings.issue: ふい alone is labeled 'the -te form of ふく'; the -te form is ふいて (the token note states this correctly: 'written here as ふい + て'). As written it teaches a wrong form label.

findings.suggested: ふいて (the -te form of ふく) + いる (the continuity auxiliary) + た (past)
findings.fix: ふいて (the -te form of ふく) + いる (the continuity auxiliary) + た (past)
notes: Wrong grammar fact: ふい is the euphonic stem, the -te form is ふいて; contradicts the token note and drops て from the decomposition.
Wrong grammar fact: ふい is the onbin stem, not the -te form (ふいて). Contradicts the record's own token note.

findings.issue: Same mislabel as expl_en: ふい sozinho não é a forma -te; a forma -te de ふく é ふいて (a note do token diz isso corretamente).

findings.issue: 出ます is called the 'masu-stem'; 出ます is the masu-FORM (the stem is 出). The swap instruction (ます→ません) is right, but the form label is wrong in a formation rule.

findings.fix: take the verb's masu-form (出ます) and change ます to ません
notes: masu-stem is 出 (as the token note itself says); calling 出ます the masu-stem breaks later rules (masu-stem + たい/ながら).
'masu-stem' conventionally means 出; the same record's token note calls 出 the stem, so labeling 出ます 'masu-stem' is internally contradictory.

findings.issue: Parenthetical '(with that)' does not correspond to anything in なんで: the record's own analysis is なん 'what' + で ('by/with'), so the literal should be 'by/with what', not the demonstrative 'that'.

findings.suggested: Why (by what)?
findings.fix: Why (by what)?
notes: 'that' is a demonstrative with no source in なんで; the record analyzes it as なん 'what' + で, so the literal must be 'by/with what'.
'(with that)' glosses なん as a demonstrative, contradicting the record's own analysis (なん = 'what'). Aligning with lit_pt's 'com quê'.

findings.issue: Mesmo problema do lit_en: '(com isso)' não corresponde a なんで; a análise do próprio registro é なん 'o quê' + で, então o literal deveria ser '(com quê)', não o demonstrativo 'isso'.
findings.current: Por que (com isso)?
findings.suggested: Por que (com quê)?
findings.fix: Por que (com quê)?
notes: Same defect as lit_en: '(com isso)' contradicts the record's own なん = 'o quê' analysis.
'(com isso)' apresenta なん como demonstrativo; a própria explicação diz なん = 'o quê'.

findings.issue: わけではない is partial negation: 'it's not that I like both (of them)' — maybe I like one. 'I don't like either' asserts total negation (neither), contradicting jp, pt and both expl fields.
findings.current: I don't like either of them.
findings.suggested: It's not that I like both of them.
findings.fix: It's not that I like both of them.
notes: わけではない denies 'I like both'; 'I don't like either' is unambiguous total negation, contradicting the jp, the pt and both explanations.
わけではない = partial denial ('not both'); 'either' forces total negation, contradicting pt, lit_en and both expl fields.

findings.issue: Same partial-negation error: 〜というわけではない means 'it's not that I like both', not 'I like neither'. The en contradicts the pt and the explanations, which correctly teach partial denial.
findings.current: I do not like either of them.
findings.suggested: It's not that I like both of them.
findings.fix: It's not that I like both of them.
notes: Same scope error with というわけではない; 'I do not like either' asserts neither, while jp/pt/expl teach partial denial.
Same scope error with というわけではない; en asserts 'neither' while pt/expl correctly teach 'it's not that I like both'.

何か as indefinite 'any' in a polite ありますか question reads なにか; なんか is casual and clashes with the register.

findings.issue: 'Both my parents are not alive' is most naturally read as 'neither is alive' (total negation); the jp わけではない is partial negation ('not both'), as pt and both expl fields correctly state.

findings.issue: 〜てほしい means the speaker wants SOMEONE ELSE to do the action, but lit_en renders it as the speaker's own action ('I want to boil'), which would be ゆでたい. Contradicts the item's own expl_en ('to want someone to do') and swaps the agent.

'I want to boil eggs' assigns the boiling to the speaker; 〜てほしい is other-agent, contradicting the entry's own pt, expl_en/pt and token note.

findings.issue: Incoherent closing note: の and もし are unrelated words, so 'の is a nominalizer, not the conditional もし' makes no sense and will confuse learners. The intended point is that the string もし inside おもしろい is not the word もし.
findings.current: Here の is a nominalizer, not the conditional もし ('if').
findings.suggested: The の is a nominalizer; note that the もし inside おもしろい is just part of the adjective, not the conditional word もし ('if').
findings.fix: 本を読む ('to read books') is a clause turned into a noun by の (nominalizer), forming 'the act of reading books'. Then は marks this block as the topic, and the predicate is the i-adjective おもしろい intensified by the adverb とても ('very'). Note that the もし inside おもしろい is just part of the adjective, not the conditional word もし ('if').
notes: Non-sequitur contrast; batch convention elsewhere (81637, 81649) explains the real false-match string.
Non-sequitur contrasting の with the unrelated word もし; the real false match is the もし inside おもしろい.

findings.issue: Same incoherent note in pt: contrasts の with もし, two unrelated words. Should clarify that the もし inside おもしろい is not the conditional word もし.

findings.fix: 本を読む ('ler livros') é uma oração transformada em substantivo pelo の (nominalizador), formando 'o ato de ler livros'. Em seguida は marca esse bloco como tópico, e o predicado é o adjetivo-i おもしろい intensificado pelo advérbio とても ('muito'). Repare que o もし dentro de おもしろい é só parte do adjetivo, não a palavra condicional もし ('se').

findings.issue: There is no suffix ～っぱい in Japanese; the intended contrast is with the homophone 一杯 (counter 杯, 'one cupful'). As written it invents a nonexistent morpheme.

findings.fix: Note that いっぱい here is the adverb 'a lot / plenty', not the counting phrase 一杯 ('one cupful', with the counter 杯).
notes: No suffix ～っぱい exists in Japanese; the statement invents a morpheme. Real contrast is the homophone 一杯 (counter 杯).
No productive suffix ～っぱい exists (the author likely meant ～っぽい or 一杯); it is an invented morpheme in a grammar note.

findings.issue: Same as expl_en: 'o sufixo ～っぱい' does not exist; the real contrast is with o homófono 一杯 (contador 杯, 'um copo cheio').

notes: Same invented morpheme '~っぱい' in the pt-BR explanation.
Same invented morpheme; but the fix must not imply the adverb is never written 一杯 — frame it as the counter reading.

findings.issue: 止め in 〜のは止めなさい ('stop doing X') is read やめ (止める=やめる, to cease an activity); とめる means to halt something in motion and is wrong with a nominalized activity. Wrong reading in context.

findings.suggested: わかっていないふりをするのわやめなさい。
findings.fix: わかっていないふりをするのわやめなさい。
notes: 〜のは止めなさい takes やめる (cease an activity); とめる (halt something in motion) is wrong with a nominalized action.
〜のは止めなさい is やめなさい (cease an activity); とめる (halt something moving) does not take a nominalized clause. Wrong in-context reading.

findings.issue: Token 止め reading とめ is wrong here; in 〜のは止めなさい the verb is やめる 'to quit/cease (an activity)', so the reading is やめ.

Same reading error at token level: 止め in 止めなさい here is やめ, not とめ.

findings.issue: Subject flipped: 君みたいに is the standard of comparison ('like you'); the implied subject who wishes to be strong is the speaker, as en, pt, lit_pt and both expl fields correctly state. 'If only you were strong' teaches the wrong parse.
findings.current: If only you were strong, huh.
findings.suggested: If (I) were strong like you, huh.
findings.fix: If (I) were strong like you, huh.
notes: 君みたいに is the standard of comparison; en, pt, lit_pt and both expl fields put the wish on the speaker. lit_en teaches the wrong parse.
君みたいに is the comparison standard; the wisher is the speaker. Current lit_en drops みたいに and flips the subject, contradicting en/pt/lit_pt/expl.

findings.issue: サボる means to deliberately skip/cut class (play hooky); 'escape from school' implies physically fleeing the premises. Also mismatches pt ('matando aula') and lit_en ('skipping school').

サボる = deliberately skip/cut class; 'escape from school' reads as physically fleeing and clashes with pt 'matando aula' and lit_en 'skipping school'.

findings.issue: Note claims 使う→使って arises by voicing ('voicing before て' / pt 'sonorização antes de て'); it is actually sokuon gemination (促音便, doubling っ). Voicing (濁音便: んで/いで) applies to ぬ/ぶ/む/ぐ verbs. Both en and pt-BR note texts are wrong.
findings.current: 使っ is the て form of 使う (voicing before て)
findings.suggested: 使っ is the て form of 使う (促音便: geminate っ before て)
findings.fix: {"en": "使っ is the て form of 使う (促音便: っ gemination before て)", "pt-BR": "使っ é a forma て de 使う (促音便: geminação em っ antes de て)"}
notes: 使う→使って is 促音便 (gemination), not voicing; 濁音便 (んで/いで) applies to ぬ/ぶ/む/ぐ verbs. Wrong grammar fact in both languages.
使う→使って is gemination (促音便), not voicing (濁音便, which is ぬ/ぶ/む/ぐ → んで/いで). Wrong grammar fact in BOTH en and pt-BR note text.

findings.issue: そう is medial deixis referring to something known/mentioned: 'like that, that way'; 'like this' corresponds to こう. expl_en itself correctly glosses it 'so/that way'.
findings.current: like this, this way
findings.suggested: like that, that way
findings.fix: like that, that way
notes: Lexical gloss must keep こう/そう deixis apart: そう = 'like that, that way'; 'like this' is こう. expl_en itself glosses it 'so/that way'.
Lexical gloss error: そう is medial ('like that'); 'like this, this way' is こう. expl_en itself glosses it 'so/that way'.

findings.issue: Same そう issue in the literal mirror: そう should be rendered 'like that', not 'like this' (that would be こう).
findings.current: They (as for them) are always like this.
findings.suggested: They (as for them) are always like that.
findings.fix: They (as for them) are always like that.
notes: 'They're always like this' is idiomatic English for いつもそうだ; the literal mirror is free-form and lit_pt ('assim') is correct. Stylistic.
'They are always like this' is idiomatic English for habitual behavior and not sense-changing; a rendering preference, unlike the lexical token gloss.

findings.issue: それ = 'that', but lit_en renders it 'this' ('On this'); the token gloss ('that') and lit_pt ('isso') treat it correctly.

notes: 'On this' is a defensible contextual rendering of それに for something at hand; token gloss ('that') and lit_pt ('isso') already carry the deixis. Over-picky.
'On this' vs 'on that' for それ is defensible in English deixis for an item under discussion; token gloss and lit_pt already carry the correct sense. Over-picky.

findings.issue: Opens with 'Same as the previous one', a dangling reference to another record; corpus sentence explanations must stand alone since sentences are stored and referenced independently.
findings.current: Same as the previous one, but with an exclamation mark: そう (so/that) + です (polite copula 'to be') as emphatic confirmation

findings.fix: そう (so/that) + です (polite copula 'to be') with an exclamation mark, as emphatic confirmation ('that's right! / exactly!'). そうです is the expression of agreement, not the 〜そうだ of report ('they say that...'), which would require a verb or adjective before it.
notes: 'Same as the previous one' is a dangling reference: corpus sentences are stored and referenced independently by ID, so explanations must stand alone.

findings.issue: Same dangling cross-record reference in Portuguese ('Igual à anterior'); the explanation must stand alone.

なさい is the command-forming auxiliary (imperative of なさる on the masu-stem), not a softener like ね/よ; en contradicts the correct pt gloss and role.

findings.issue: タルティーヌ is mis-romanized as "tarutei-nu": ティー is phonetically "tii" (long i), not "tei" plus hyphen. Not covered by the known unromanized-katakana issue since it was romanized, but wrongly.

findings.suggested: watashiwatarutiinuwajamuonuttetaberu.
findings.fix: watashiwatarutiinuwajamuonuttetaberu.
notes: てぃ romanizes as "ti", not "tei"; "tarutei-nu" teaches a wrong pronunciation of タルティーヌ.
Systemic romanizer convention, not a per-sentence defect: ー→'-' is corpus-wide (ko-hi-, bi-ru) and てぃ→'tei' in all 7 パーティー cases (pa-tei-); the fix would break consistency.

findings.issue: 出たところだった is past-in-past ('had just left'). The en uses present perfect, contradicting the pt ('tinha acabado de sair') and the expl fields, which explicitly teach that だった puts the 'just did' into the past.

findings.fix: The bus had just left.
notes: en is verbatim Layer-A Tatoeba pair (jpn 9953034 -> eng 35302 'The bus has just left.'). Past framing is carried by pt/lit_en/expl; loose tense in source pair is not a defect.
だった makes it past-in-past; en contradicts pt ('tinha acabado de sair') and both expl fields, which teach exactly this contrast.

のはどう is a suggestion and てみる is dropped; current en reads as a real why-question, contradicting pt/lit_en/expl.
